imp.generic: She decided to buy the flowers herself.
imp.author: Mrs. Dalloway said she would buy the flowers herself; for Lucy had her work cut out for her; the doors would be taken off their hinges; and then, thought Clarissa, what a morning -- fresh as if issued to children on a beach.

imp.generic: It was a fresh, calm morning and the air felt nice.
imp.author: How fresh, how calm, stiller than this of course, the air was in the early morning; like the flap of a wave; the kiss of a wave; chill and sharp and yet (for a girl of eighteen as she then was) solemn.

imp.generic: London is a busy city full of different kinds of people.
imp.author: For nothing was simply one thing -- the city pressed and swarmed, a thousand lives brushing against one another, each sealed, each entire, each dissolving at the edges into the next.

imp.generic: She thought about her past as she grew older.
imp.author: The past, she found, did not recede; it accumulated, pressing forward the older one grew, so that the girl of eighteen was not gone but everywhere at once, in windows, in the smell of cut grass, in a little squeak of the hinges she could hear now.

It was precisely twelve o'clock; twelve by Big Ben; whose stroke was wafted over the northern part of London; blent with that of other clocks, mixed in a thin ethereal way with the clouds and wisps of smoke, and died up there among the seagulls. The leaden circles dissolved in the air.

imp.generic: He did not understand her, and she knew it.
imp.author: He looked at her with great kindness, which was worse, in its way, than indifference -- for behind the kindness was a complete and settled incomprehension, as final as a wall.

imp.generic: She often did things to impress other people, which was foolish.
imp.author: Half the time she did things not simply, not for themselves; but to make people think this or that; perfect idiocy she knew (and now the policeman held up his hand) for no one was ever for a second taken in.

imp.generic: She walked into the room and everyone noticed her.
imp.author: She had that quality -- one could not name it, exactly -- of making the room rearrange itself around her arrival, the conversations tilting, the flowers on the table suddenly more themselves.

imp.generic: The kitchen was full of dishes and cooking equipment.
imp.author: It made no difference to Mrs. Walker among the plates, saucepans, cullenders, frying-pans, chicken in aspic, ice-cream freezers, pared crusts of bread, lemons, soup tureens, and pudding basins which, however hard they washed up, seemed to be all on top of her.

imp.generic: In conclusion, life is full of small, meaningful moments.
imp.author: It was this, then -- not the great passages, not the arrivals and catastrophes, but the cup set down, the squeak of a hinge, the light moving across the floor -- that constituted, if anything did, a life.
